model_assumptions: DXOMARK displayed matrix is treated as WB-normalized native-column to linear-sRGB-column, followed by inverse Bradford adaptation to the reference illuminant. This convention is an interpretation checked for neutral consistency, not verified against DXOMARK's raw processing code.
Sony A/D50 and Hasselblad A/D65 characterize different devices with independent fitted data; common XYZ is a model-mediated bridge, not a paired dual-light measurement.
External Hasselblad chart targets were Bradford-adapted reference patches, not spectral reflectance integrals under measured DPReview illuminant SPDs.
A constant left residual anchors the public response family to the existing paired calibration; its transfer across illuminants is assumed.
Stored XYZ-to-camera matrices interpolate in inverse Kelvin; outside each camera's own endpoints they clamp. No Sony D65 measurement is fabricated.
Neutral scalar normalization retains the existing calibration exposure. Full Phocus RAW equivalence and arbitrary LED accuracy are unverified.
limitations: Captures are from 2022 and 2025; scene/illuminant changes remain confounded with sensor response.
One illumination and 24 patches cannot establish cross-scene or cross-illuminant accuracy.
Factory normal non-HDR colour path at unit effective gain; no per-unit closed-loop calibration or Phocus spatial processing.
LibRaw AHD decoding and chart exposure anchor differ from Phocus's RAW decoding/exposure chain; actual TIFF comparison is documented separately.
